transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today. I, um... well, it feels a little silly to admit, especially being a teacher and supposed to be the responsible adult, but I've been having some trouble with... well, with spiders. I hope that's the sort of thing you can help with? 

It's just getting to the point where I'm sort of arranging my own house around not seeing them, which I know sounds a bit ridiculous. I'll put off doing the laundry for days because it's down in the basement, or I'll completely avoid my garden shed. I've even started paying people to do small handyman jobs around the house that I know perfectly well how to do myself, just because I can't quite make myself go into those spaces where they might be. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Are you avoiding those places mainly because you're worried about seeing spiders, or is it more about feeling trapped or anxious in those spaces in general?

Oh, no, it's definitely the spiders. I don't mind the basement or the shed at all otherwise. I mean, I know it's silly. I know a little spider sitting in the corner of my old house isn't actually going to hurt me. I'm an educated woman, I know they're more scared of me than I am of them. 

But... well, it's just that the moment I even picture one dropping out of a box I'm moving, or just sitting there near the washing machine, it just... it feels enormous and threatening in a way that I'm honestly a bit embarrassed to admit to you. I know it sounds like an overreaction, but I just can't seem to help it. Is that... is that normal for people who come to see you?
When you feel this fear, is it specifically about actual spiders, or does it also happen if you see something that looks like a spider, like a spider costume, a toy spider, or even a drawing of one?

Oh, well... no, I suppose it's really just the actual spiders. I mean, if I see a drawing in a textbook or a plastic one around Halloween, I might not love it, but I don't get that awful panicked feeling. I know it's not real, so it doesn't bother me nearly as much. 

I guess I'm fairly practical about it when it's just a picture or a toy. It's really just the live ones, the way they move, that gets to me. I hope that's the right answer? I don't want to sound like I'm frightened of absolutely everything, because I'm really not. I'm usually quite sensible!

latest_inference.note: The patient clarified that her fear is specifically about live spiders and the way they move, rather than images, toys, or costumes. This rules out other specific phobia types and supports a more specific diagnosis of spider phobia.
